mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months signals a shift toward monetary easing, lowering discount rates and increasing present-value weights on future cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of macro easing episodes, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.25% triggers a risk-off cascade, compressing discount rates and reducing the present value of equity cash flows, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 60% of rate hike episodes, or walk-forward Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns in > 60% of strong-labor episodes, or walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below -10,000 jobs signals a weakening labor market, which raises uncertainty and compresses discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in > 60% of weak-labor episodes, or walk-forward Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year window.
